cards.explanation: The answer is that they are opposites that don't mix. Righteousness and wickedness, light and darkness: Paul sets them side by side and asks what partnership or fellowship they could possibly have. The questions answer themselves, because nothing. That's the point he's making when he says not to be unequally yoked with unbelievers (2 Corinthians 6:14).

The answer is that we believers ourselves are the temple of the living God. Paul says, "For we are the temple of the living God." Not a building, but the people. Makes me stand up a little straighter on my gold base, friends (2 Corinthians 6:16).

The answer is True. God says, "I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people." Dwell with them AND walk among them, friends. That's a God who promises to live right there with His people (2 Corinthians 6:16).

The answer is that the Lord calls His people to come out from among them and be separate. He says, "Therefore come out from among them and be separate, says the Lord." That "Therefore" ties it to everything before it, to the temple and to God dwelling with His people. It's a call to come out and be separate (2 Corinthians 6:17).

The answer is False. The Lord says, "Touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you." Turned away? Go look for it, friends, because it's not in that line. The only door in that sentence is the one swinging open to receive them. I've been shut in a drawer, so believe me, I notice an open door (2 Corinthians 6:17).

The answer is a Father. The Lord says, "I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty." A Father, with sons and daughters in the very same line. I know a thing or two about being called Papa, and it's the best name I've got (2 Corinthians 6:18).

The answer is holiness. Paul says, "…let us cleanse ourselves from everything that defiles body and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God." Holiness is what gets perfected, friends. It's a whole-kitchen kind of cleaning, and it starts with the promises Paul just listed (2 Corinthians 7:1).
